style.vernacular: Pyrenean stone: farmhouses and churches of irregular local granite and slate stone, lime-rendered facades, steep double-pitch roofs of grey slate slabs (llicorella), timber balconies and bell towers or bellcotes; the Romanesque church tradition lasted late here. The valley floor towns (Andorra la Vella, Escaldes) are dense with 1960s-2000s concrete, render and glass blocks, spa and shopping buildings; ski villages (Pas de la Casa, Soldeu, Arinsal) mix chalet-style timber and stone with tall apartment blocks. Conifer forest and bare high pastures above.
style.ornament: Square stone bell towers with round-arched belfry openings and pyramidal slate roofs; Lombard bands and bellcotes (espadanya) on small chapels; small oculus under the gable apex; timber balconies and iron balcony railings on casas; wrought-iron grilles from the Ordino forges; stone-and-slate chalet styling in ski villages.

sources.what: Romanesque dominance in the Pyrenees, churches (Sant Joan de Caselles, Santa Coloma, Sant Esteve), Casa de la Vall, old town 15th-early 20th c., Baroque examples
irregular local stone walls, lime-rendered main facade, double-pitched slate-slab roof, bellcote
irregular stonework in clay mortar, llicorella slate roof, square bell tower with four-pitched roof
